rationale: History (simulator estimates only, never hardware; Metal numerically checked the exact source/config/TIR while the CUDA binary was not executed; no global-optimality claim): attempt-00 32x64x32 s3 = 147.72us, attempt-01 32x64x64 s2 = 147.67us (best so far), attempt-02 32x128x32 s3 = 148.28us, attempt-03 32x128x64 s1 = 196.54us (clear regression), attempt-04 32x64x32 s2 = 147.70us. All these block_N=64, num_stages in {2,3} tuples cluster tightly around ~147.7us, whereas block_N=128 and num_stages=1 are consistently worse. Therefore narrow block_N to [64] and num_stages to [2,3] to concentrate exploration on the promising band, keep block_K=[32,64] (64 already best in attempt-01), and keep block_M=[32] since 64/128 do not divide M=32; all domains remain nonempty and HiGHS will still avoid cap-violating tuples (e.g., block_N=64, block_K=64, s3 would need 36864 bytes > 32768). Constraints: tiles divide M=32,N=4096,K=4096; shared_bytes=max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages, 4*block_M*block_N) <= 32768 plus the hard 32768-byte portability cap. Weights keep traffic/pipeline/footprint at 1.5 and launches at 0.25 since M=32 already limits grid; footprint remains to penalize smem-tight tuples after attempt-02/03 regressions. Next hypothesis: with block_N fixed at 64 and stages restricted to {2,3}, the remaining unexplored tuple is 32x64x64 s3, which the shared cap excludes; among allowed tuples the solver should pick block_K=64 s2 or block_K=32 s3, so this round tests whether the best ~147.67us can be beaten by a stage-3 alternative; if not, we will consider slightly raising the shared cap only if actual compiled smem still fits, or re-broadening block_N once block_K/stage effects are better isolated.
